title: Payment Operations Note: Mail-Float Relief on a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Late-Posted Installment Charge
content:
**Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract — customers who pay by mailed check.**

**Rule.** When the contract shows a payment by mailed check posted in the last 2 calendar months and the contract is not enrolled in autopay, the charge figured at the rate is halved and the result rounded down to the whole dollar; when it shows such a mailed check payment and the contract is enrolled in autopay, the charge figured at the rate is multiplied by three quarters and the result rounded down to the whole dollar; in every other case the charge figured at the rate is kept to the cent.

The charge figured at the rate is the late charge computed on one monthly payment at the rate that applies, rounded to the cent, before the late-charge cap; the cap then applies to the figure this rule produces.

**Records and counting.** A payment by mailed check is a payment entry on the contract's ledger whose channel is mailed check; autopay enrolment is read from the contract record. Whole calendar months from one date to a later one are the difference in month numbers, less one when the later date's day number is smaller than the earlier date's, with no month-end adjustment; an entry lies in the last N calendar months when its date is not after today and fewer than N whole months run from its date to today, which is the same as being dated after the same day number N months before today.

| Mailed check payment in the last 2 calendar months | Enrolled in autopay | Figure carried to the cap |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | half, rounded down to the whole dollar |
| yes | yes | three quarters, rounded down to the whole dollar |
| no | either | the charge at the rate, to the cent |

## Worked cases (hypothetical inputs)

A charge figured at the rate of 15.47 dollars and a mailed check that posted five weeks ago: without autopay, half is 7.735, rounded down to 7.00 dollars; with autopay, three quarters is 11.6025, rounded down to 11.00 dollars. A mailed check dated the same day number two months before today is outside the window, and the charge stays 15.47 dollars.
